st.2: They built true arches, not merely corbelled ones.
st.1: Wells, drains and coined money were known.
st.3: The assembly hall at Harappa had 20 pillars.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – wells, drains and bows-and-arrows were known, but not coined money; 2 – they built only corbelled arches, never the true arch; 3 – the 20-pillared assembly hall is at Mohenjodaro; 4 – iron was unknown to them.

st.2: Carnelian came from Badakhshan in Afghanistan.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – iron was unknown to the Harappans and was not a bead material; 2 – carnelian came from Saurashtra / Bharuch (Badakhshan supplied lapis lazuli).

st.3: The Kazipet inscription names Beta Raja I as the first Kakatiya king.

x: All three statements are correct: Kalamalla (Renati Chodas) is the first Telugu inscription, Magallu first mentions the Kakatiyas, and Kazipet names Beta Raja I as the first Kakatiya king.

st.2: It is described as composed in five stages ending in the 5th century BCE.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – its five stages began in the 5th century BCE and ran on to about the 12th century CE; 3 – about one lakh verses in 18 books describes the Mahabharata.

st.2: Pakudha Kachchayana of this list is Mahavira.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 – Mahavira is Nigantha Nataputta, not Pakudha Kachchayana; 4 – Makkhali Gosala taught Niyativada (fatalism), while Akriyavada was Purana Kassapa's doctrine.

st.2: A fully liberated soul is called a Ganadhara.
st.4: Jainism accepts the authority of the Vedas.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – a fully liberated soul is a Siddha (Ganadharas are the chief disciples of a Tirthankara); 3 – salvation requires the monastic life; 4 – Jainism rejects the authority of the Vedas.

st.1: Under Chandragupta Maurya, prince Susima failed to put down the Taxila revolt.
st.4: Ashoka had served as viceroy at Taxila and Tosali.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – the revolt Susima failed to quell was under Bindusara; 3 – the later revolt in Ashoka's reign was handled by Kunala; 4 – Ashoka was viceroy at Taxila and Ujjain (Tosali lay in Kalinga, conquered only in his reign).

st.3: His coronation took place in 269 BCE, about four years after his accession.

x: All three statements are correct: the Samantapasadika says he won Avanti in Bindusara's time, the Mahavamsa speaks of 99 brothers killed, and he was crowned in 269 BCE after a four-year gap following accession (c. 273 BCE).

st.1: He was the envoy of Antiochus I and wrote the Indica.
st.2: He divided Indian society into seven classes, of which the soldiers were the most numerous.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – he was the envoy of Seleucus Nikator (Deimachus came from Antiochus I); 2 – of his seven classes the cultivators were the most numerous; 3 – his two types of philosophers were Brahmins and Sramanas.

st.2: His capital was Ujjain.

x: Neither statement is correct. 1 – defeating the Sakas and issuing silver coins belongs to Chandragupta II; 2 – Chandragupta I ruled from Pataliputra.

st.1: Most Gupta coins were of silver, gold coins being issued only rarely.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 – most Gupta coins were gold dinaras; 4 – the king-queen type was issued by Chandragupta I.

st.3: Durga, Amba, Kali and Chandi were worshipped as forms of Lakshmi, the consort of Vishnu.
st.1: The Kalamukha sect, the oldest Shaiva sect, was founded by Lakulisha.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – the oldest Shaiva sect founded by Lakulisha is the Pashupata; 2 – the Kapalikas were an extremist Shaiva sect; 3 – Durga, Amba, Kali and Chandi were worshipped as mother goddesses (forms of Shakti), not of Lakshmi.

st.1: It is an Upapurana, not one of the 18 Mahapuranas.

x: All three statements are correct: the Kalika Purana is an Upapurana of Shaktism, likely composed in Assam.

st.2: Aditya I founded the imperial Chola line by capturing Tanjore.
st.1: Rajaraja I succeeded Rajendra I on the Chola throne.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. 1 – Rajaraja I was the father and predecessor of Rajendra I; 2 – the imperial Chola line was founded by Vijayalaya, who captured Tanjore; Aditya I was his successor. The order is Vijayalaya, Aditya I, Rajaraja I, Rajendra I.

st.1: Abdullah Khan was the Wazir and Husain Ali Khan the Mir Bakhshi.

x: All three statements are correct: Abdullah Khan was Wazir and Husain Ali Khan Mir Bakhshi; they were eliminated under Muhammad Shah with Nizam-ul-Mulk's help; and the 1719 grant gave Balaji Vishwanath chauth and sardeshmukhi of the six Deccan subas.

st.3: The charbagh, the four-quartered garden, was introduced by Humayun.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – pietra dura began under Jahangir (tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah), before the Taj Mahal; 3 – the charbagh was introduced by Babur.

st.1: Vemana's verses are mostly in the Kanda metre with the refrain 'Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema'.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – Vemana's verses are mostly in the Ataveladi metre; 3 – Siddaiah was a Muslim (Dudekula); it was Kakkaiah who was a Madiga.

st.1: Schulz began the translation in 1719 and only learnt Telugu from 1727.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – he learnt Telugu from 1719 and began the translation in 1727, not the other way round; 3 – it was printed at Halle in 1746-47, not at Serampore.

st.3: Pondicherry was transferred to India in 1954 and renamed Puducherry in 1962.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – the Masulipatnam patent (1669) came from the Sultan of Golconda, not the Mughal emperor; 3 – Pondicherry was renamed Puducherry in 2006.

st.1: It was led by Lord North.
st.2: The judicial murder of Nand Kumar was not among the charges.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – the impeachment was led by Edmund Burke; 2 – the judicial murder of Nand Kumar was one of the charges; 3 – the trial ended in his acquittal in 1795.

st.2: The Act of 1767 obliged the Company to pay the Mughal emperor £400,000 a year.
st.1: The Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa was granted in 1765 by Shuja-ud-Daula.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. 1 – the Diwani was granted by the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II; 2 – the 1767 Act made the Company pay £400,000 a year to the British treasury; 3 – the dividend was capped at 10 per cent in 1767.

st.2: Munro's collectorate and tahsildari schools were closed in 1836.

x: All three statements are correct: Munro's 1826 survey found a wide network of village schools, his collectorate and tahsildari schools were closed in 1836 after the 1835 resolution, and English replaced Persian as official language in 1837.

st.2: Gurajada Apparao, not Veeresalingam, was the first to render Sanskrit dramas such as Abhijnana Sakuntalam and Ratnavali into Telugu.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – it was Veeresalingam himself who first rendered Abhijnana Sakuntalam, Ratnavali and other Sanskrit dramas into Telugu; 3 – it was Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri, not Kokkonda Venkataratnam, who called Rajasekhara Charitra a mere translation.

st.4: Annie Besant set the tune of the 'Morning Song of India'.
st.3: Rabindranath Tagore translated 'Jana Gana Mana' into English there as 'Morning Song of India' in 1911.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – the first principal was James H. Cousins, not Jiddu Krishnamurti; 3 – Tagore wrote the song in 1911 but translated it at Madanapalle in February 1919; 4 – the tune was set by Margaret Cousins.

st.2: The Khilafat Committee was formed at Lucknow in 1919 under the lead of the Ali brothers.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – the Khilafat Committee was formed at Bombay in 1919; 3 – Mustafa Kemal abolished the Caliphate in 1924, not 1922.

st.3: Its secretary was Unnava Lakshminarayana.

x: All three statements are correct: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was president, Unnava Lakshminarayana secretary (Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was treasurer), and the Pithapuram Raja's People's Party backed the Swarajists.

st.1: The Ramgarh session of 1940 was the 53rd session of the Congress, presided over by Rajendra Prasad.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – the Ramgarh session was presided over by Maulana Azad; 2 – it was held in March 1940, before the August Offer.

st.2: Jawaharlal Nehru was the chairman of the National Planning Committee set up in 1938 under Bose's presidency.

x: All three statements are correct: Tripuri is near Jabalpur, Nehru chaired the 1938 National Planning Committee set up under Bose's presidency, and Bose favoured the Roman script for Hindustani.

st.2: The Khosla Commission (1970) concluded that he died in the air crash.

x: All three statements are correct: the Shah Nawaz Committee and the Khosla Commission held that he died in the crash, while the Mukherjee Commission held that he did not.

st.1: The Governor-General of each dominion was to be appointed by the British King on the advice of the British cabinet.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – the Governor-General was appointed on the advice of the dominion cabinet; 2 – the Constituent Assembly could repeal the Independence Act, and India's did so through Article 395.

st.1: Manda Suryanarayana, who presided over the Vizag district meeting of June 1913, was the municipal chairman of Vizianagaram.

x: All three statements are correct: Manda Suryanarayana, municipal chairman of Vizianagaram, presided at the June 1913 meeting; the Guntur Youngmen's Literary Association (1903) is the cradle of the movement; and Vinjamuri Bhavanacharyulu presided over the 1912-13 committee.

st.1: The Constitution, as it came into force on 26 January 1950, included a separate Andhra State.

x: Neither statement is correct. Andhra State was formed only on 1 October 1953, after the Constitution came into force, so the 1950 Constitution had no separate Andhra State.

st.1: The Mulki rules date from 1888 and were tightened by the Nizam's farman of 1919.

x: All three statements are correct: the Mulki rules date from 1888 and were tightened by the 1919 farman; the 1952 agitation under Burgula saw firing near City College; and Justice Pingali Jaganmohan Reddy inquired into it.

st.2: The Communist daily 'Visalandhra' was started in June 1952.

x: All three statements are correct: Sundarayya coined 'Visalandhra' and wrote Visalandhralo Prajarajyam, the daily Visalandhra began in June 1952, and he became the first General Secretary of the CPI(M) in 1964.

st.1: Langhnaj is in Rajasthan.
st.4: Chopani Mando in the Son valley has huts and microliths.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – Langhnaj is in Gujarat; 3 – Paisra is in Bihar (Munger), not West Bengal; 4 – Chopani Mando is in the Belan valley.

st.3: The Gathasaptasati is a Maharashtri Prakrit anthology of 700 verses.

x: All three statements are correct: Srinatha's works describe Reddi-period sea trade, the Gathasaptasati preserves early Telugu words, and it is a Maharashtri Prakrit anthology of 700 verses.

st.2: They were generally in Sanskrit.

x: Neither statement is correct. 1 – the legends were in Brahmi, not Kharosthi; 2 – they were generally in Prakrit, not Sanskrit.

st.4: Bhutapala funded the great chaitya hall at Nasik.
st.1: Kings and ministers, not queens and women, are the first among donors in the inscriptions.
st.3: An Amaravati relief shows the ivory-worker Dimikudu offering a Purnakumbha.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – queens and women come first among the donors; 2 – the guilds named at Amaravati were of ivory workers, not goldsmiths; 3 – Dimikudu was a leather-worker; 4 – Bhutapala funded the great chaitya hall at Karle.

st.2: Percy Brown called Amaravati art the 'epitome of Indian architecture'.

x: Neither statement is correct. 1 – 'Tree and Serpent Worship' was written by James Fergusson; 2 – 'epitome of Indian architecture' is Fergusson's phrase; Percy Brown spoke of its 'dynamic beauty'.

st.1: Vengi became independent under the Eastern Chalukyas in 624 CE, with Rajahmundry as capital.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – the first Eastern Chalukya capital was Pithapuram (Rajahmundry became capital much later); 2 – Pulakesin II took the title Paramesvara after defeating Harsha, not Mahendravarman I.

st.4: He took the throne after his brother Bhima Salki died without an heir.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 – the 108 temples are recorded in the Sataluru inscription (the Addanki inscription belongs to Gunaga Vijayaditya III); 4 – he took the throne by overthrowing his brother Bhima Salki.

st.1: The chapters of the Ramayana are called Parvas, those of the Mahabharata Kandas.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. 1 – the Ramayana's chapters are Kandas and the Mahabharata's Parvas, not the reverse; 2 – in Virata's kingdom Yudhishthira took the name Kanka (Vallabha was Bhima's name).

st.2: She was the fourth sovereign ruler of the Kakatiya line.

x: All three statements are correct: she was co-regent from 1258 as Rudradeva Maharaja, the fourth sovereign Kakatiya (after Rudradeva, Mahadeva and Ganapatideva), and the second great woman ruler of medieval India after Razia Sultana.

st.2: Devaraya I hired 10,000 Muslim soldiers and gave them jagirs.
st.1: Devaraya II was the first Vijayanagara ruler to appoint Muslims in the army.

x: Neither statement is correct. 1 – the first to appoint Muslims in the army was Devaraya I; 2 – the 10,000 Muslim soldiers given jagirs were hired by Devaraya II.

st.1: Amaram was land granted to Brahmins as a tax-free religious gift.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – amaram was land granted to military chiefs in place of a cash salary; 2 – the amaranayakas had more autonomy than the Durgadannayakas.

st.1: It was written by Palkuriki Somanatha.
st.2: It portrays Vijayanagara as an abode of drama artists.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – the Kridabhiramam was written by Vinukonda Vallabharaya; 2 – it portrays Orugallu (Warangal), not Vijayanagara, as an abode of drama artists; 3 – 'A Lover's Guide to Warangal' is the English translation by V. Narayana Rao and David Shulman (Jayapa Senani wrote the Nritta Ratnavali).

st.2: The Madras Native Association petitioned against it in 1861.

x: All three statements are correct: Moturpha was a tax on looms, shops and other trades, it was attacked in the Madras Native Association's 1861 petition, and it was abolished in 1861.

st.2: 'Maa Telugu Talliki' is his song regarded as the first Telugu national song.
st.1: He is called 'Kavi Samrat'.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. 1 – he is called the first Telugu national poet; 'Kavi Samrat' is Viswanatha Satyanarayana's title; 2 – his 'Hinduvulara ennaallee gati' is the first Telugu national song, while 'Maa Telugu Talliki' was written by Sankarambadi Sundarachari.

st.2: He was jailed for the play 'Kanyasulkam'.
st.3: He was the first Andhra leader to join M.N. Roy's Radical Democratic Party and led its Andhra branch.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – he was jailed for the playlet 'Chichula Pidugu' (Kanyasulkam is Gurajada's play); 3 – he was the first Andhra leader in Bose's Forward Bloc and led its Andhra branch; 4 – he did not found an Andhra Swaraj Party in 1934 – after the Salt Satyagraha he joined the Congress Socialist Party.

st.3: In July 2026, at the Borra Caves, Andhra Pradesh announced an annual Telugu Mahotsavam and the revival of the Nandi Natakotsavams.
st.1: The Harikatha artist Miriyala Apparao was given the Padma Shri (posthumous) in 2025.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – Miriyala Apparao was a Burrakatha artist; 3 – the announcement was made at the Undavalli Caves (27 July 2026); 4 – Dalavai Chalapathi Rao received the Padma Shri in 2020.

st.2: It was founded by Kshetrayya.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 – Kuchipudi was founded by Siddhendra Yogi (Kshetrayya was a composer of padams); 4 – the village was gifted by Abul Hasan Tana Shah.

st.3: Arrack was prohibited from 1 October 1993 by the Kotla Vijayabhaskara Reddy government.

x: All three statements are correct: the movement began at Dubagunta (Nellore) in 1991 under Rosamma, grew out of the Aksharajyothi classes, and arrack was banned from 1 October 1993 by the Kotla Vijayabhaskara Reddy government (NTR's total prohibition came in 1995).

st.1: The ancestors of the Sungas came from Taxila.
st.2: Agnimitra, son of Pushyamitra, was viceroy at Pataliputra.

x: Neither statement is correct. 1 – the ancestors of the Sungas came from Ujjain; 2 – Agnimitra was viceroy at Vidisha.

st.1: Besides Adivaraha, he bore the title 'Maharajadhiraja of Aryavarta'.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 – his second title was Prabhasa ('Maharajadhiraja of Aryavarta' was Mahendrapala I); 4 – his Gwalior prashasti was composed by Baladitya (Rajashekhara was at Mahendrapala I's court).

st.3: Population carries a 15–25% weight in Finance Commission formulas.

x: All three statements are correct: India needs jobs for about 9.7 million new working-age people a year, population growth shrinks land holdings, and population has a 15–25% weight in Finance Commission formulas.

st.1: Andre Beteille described caste as cumulative inequality and class as dispersed inequality.

x: All three statements are correct: Beteille saw caste as cumulative and class as dispersed inequality; Dumont and Pocock founded Contributions to Indian Sociology in 1957; and Maine described the movement from status to contract.

st.1: In the Later Vedic period Swayamvara declined and widow remarriage was discouraged.

x: All three statements are correct: in the Later Vedic period Swayamvara declined and widow remarriage was discouraged; the Satyashodhak marriage had no dowry or Brahmin priest; and niyoga allowed a wife to beget a child by a designated man.

st.2: Amalgamation refers to the fusion of distinct groups and cultures into a new one.

x: All three statements are correct: acculturation leaves the group distinct, amalgamation is fusion into a new group (peaceful coexistence is cultural pluralism), and an ethnic group shares a common culture.

st.4: Youth dormitories are a feature of caste-based peasant society, not of tribal society.
st.1: Verrier Elwin described the Hindu method of tribal absorption.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – the Hindu method of tribal absorption was described by N.K. Bose (Elwin argued for isolation); 2 – the tribe-caste continuum was proposed by Surajit Sinha, not T.K. Oommen; 4 – youth dormitories are a typical feature of tribal society.

st.1: Khasi belongs to the Austro-Asiatic family and Garo to the Sino-Tibetan family.

x: All three statements are correct: Khasi is Austro-Asiatic (Mon-Khmer) and Garo Sino-Tibetan (Bodo), the 2011 Census recorded 121 languages and 270 mother tongues, and the Jains were notified as a minority in 2014.

st.3: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 replaced the Special Marriage Act and fixes 18 years for females and 21 for males.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. 1 – the PCPNDT Act, 1994 came into force on 1 January 1996; 3 – the 2006 Act replaced the Sarda (Child Marriage Restraint) Act, 1929.

st.1: Hate speech is specifically defined in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. 1 – hate speech is not specifically defined in Indian law; 3 – IPC Section 295A corresponds to BNS Section 299.

st.4: The demands for Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Telangana illustrate linguistic identity as a cause of regionalism.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 – the Gorkhas in Bengal illustrate fear of losing cultural identity; 4 – Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Telangana illustrate political neglect, not linguistic identity.

st.1: The Gurupadaswamy Committee on child labour was set up in 1979 by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. 1 – the committee was set up by the Ministry of Labour; 3 – its recommendations led to the National Policy on Child Labour, 1987.

st.2: Andhra Pradesh's NTR Bharosa Pension gives Rs 4,000 a month to widows and the elderly, but not to transgender persons.

x: Neither statement is correct. 1 – Census 2011 counted about 4.88 lakh transgender persons, the highest in Uttar Pradesh; 2 – the NTR Bharosa Pension of Rs 4,000 a month also covers transgender persons.

st.1: Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947, before the tribal invasion began.
st.2: Indian troops were airlifted on 25 October 1947, a day before the Instrument was signed.
st.4: India referred the Kashmir issue to the UN General Assembly on 1 January 1948 under Article 35 of the UN Charter.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – the Instrument was signed on 26 October 1947 after the tribal invasion; 2 – troops were airlifted on 27 October, after the signing; 3 – only defence, external affairs and communications were ceded, land revenue stayed with the State; 4 – India referred the issue to the UN Security Council.

st.2: The Johnson Line of 1865 places Aksai Chin in Xinjiang and represents China's claim.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – China rejects the McMahon Line; 2 – the Johnson Line places Aksai Chin in Ladakh and represents India's claim.

st.1: The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra is conducted through the Lipulekh and Shipki La passes.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. 1 – the Yatra goes through Lipulekh and Nathu La; 2 – the AIIB is headquartered in Beijing.

st.2: In the Kulbhushan Jadhav case (2019) the ICJ held that Pakistan had breached the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations.

x: All three statements are correct: Nagendra Singh was ICJ President in 1985-88, the Jadhav judgment found a breach of the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, and the climate advisory opinion of July 2025 was unanimous.

st.1: It began operations in January 2014.
st.3: India is its largest shareholder and China the second-largest.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. 1 – the AIIB began operations in January 2016; 2 – the USA and Japan are not members; 3 – China is the largest shareholder and India the second-largest.

st.1: The second Ministerial Conference (1998) was held at Geneva.

x: All three statements are correct: the second conference (1998) was at Geneva (Singapore hosted the first, 1996), Seattle and Cancún broke down, and the Doha Development Agenda was launched at the fourth conference in 2001.

st.3: India avoids BRICS de-dollarisation.

x: All three statements are correct: Argentina was invited in August 2023 but declined in December 2023, BRICS now has ten members, and India avoids de-dollarisation.

st.3: The first AIKEYME exercise with African navies was held in Kenya in 2025.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – Japan became a permanent Malabar partner in 2015 (Australia rejoined in 2020); 3 – the first AIKEYME was held in Tanzania (Dar es Salaam) in 2025.

st.3: The term 'basic structure' does not appear anywhere in the Constitution; it was evolved by the judiciary.

x: All three statements are correct: 'secular' came with the 42nd Amendment, Fundamental Duties were absent in 1950, and 'basic structure' is a judicial doctrine not written into the Constitution.

st.1: Reserved subjects were administered by the Governor with his Executive Council, who were answerable to the legislature.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. 1 – the Governor and his Executive Council were not answerable to the legislature for reserved subjects; 3 – irrigation was a reserved subject.

st.1: It is linked with Article 31C.
st.2: It was the first Schedule added to the Constitution, by the Fourth Amendment, 1955.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – the Ninth Schedule is linked with Article 31B; 2 – it was added by the First Amendment, 1951; 4 – it originally contained 13 Acts.

st.2: It removed the residence requirement for naturalisation of the covered communities altogether.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 – it reduced the residence requirement to five years, not removed it; 4 – its validity is challenged mainly under Article 14.

st.1: An arrested person must be told the grounds of arrest, but may consult only a lawyer assigned by the State.
st.4: In Vihaan Kumar v. State of Haryana (2025), the Supreme Court said the grounds need be communicated only if the arrestee asks for them.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – the arrestee may consult a lawyer of his choice; 2 – the safeguards do not cover civil arrest or the deportation of an alien; 4 – the Court held that grounds must be meaningfully communicated to every arrestee.

st.2: In January 2026, the Supreme Court agreed to examine whether the Enforcement Directorate can invoke writ jurisdiction, in appeals by Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

x: All three statements are correct: an HC dismissal on merits bars the same plea under Article 32, the ED writ question (January 2026) arose in appeals by Kerala and Tamil Nadu, and the SOP for 24x7 urgent hearings was studied in July 2026.

st.3: Under its three-tier set-up, Human Rights Courts function at the district level.

x: All three statements are correct: the NHRC was constituted on 12 October 1993, the Act is deemed in force from 28 September 1993, and Human Rights Courts function at the district level.

st.2: Uttar Pradesh was the first State to implement the 10 per cent EWS quota, from 14 January 2019.
st.1: EWS eligibility requires family income below Rs 8 lakh, with no limit on agricultural land.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. 1 – besides income below Rs 8 lakh, agricultural land must be below 5 acres; 2 – Gujarat was the first State to implement it; 3 – Janhit Abhiyan was decided 3:2 by a five-judge bench.

st.2: It has a Chairperson and six members, including at least four women.
st.4: Kailash Satyarthi was its first Chairperson.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – the six members must include at least two women; 3 – it has the powers of a civil court, not a criminal court; 4 – its first Chairperson was Shantha Sinha.

st.2: The 86th Amendment substituted Article 46.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – the 86th Amendment substituted Article 45 (early childhood care); 3 – Article 44 (uniform civil code) was in the original Constitution; the 42nd Amendment added Articles 39A, 43A and 48A.

st.3: The duty in Article 51A(g) came in after the 1992 Rio Earth Summit.
st.1: The 42nd Amendment, which inserted them, came into force on 26 January 1977.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – the 42nd Amendment came into force on 3 January 1977; 3 – Article 51A(g) came in 1976, after the 1972 Stockholm Conference; 4 – the eleventh duty was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

st.1: They are criticised as too exhaustive, since they even include duties such as voting.
st.4: Courts cannot use them to assess the reasonableness of laws.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – they are criticised as not exhaustive, as they omit duties such as voting and paying taxes; 3 – critics object that they are appended to Part IV instead of following Part III; 4 – courts do use them to judge the reasonableness of laws.

st.1: Article 13(4) was inserted by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – Article 13(4) was inserted by the 24th Amendment, 1971; 3 – the amendment procedure was borrowed from South Africa.

st.3: The word 'Cabinet' appears in Article 352.

x: All three statements are correct: the Council of Ministers rarely meets as a body, the Cabinet directs it, and the word 'Cabinet' appears only in Article 352 (inserted by the 44th Amendment), not in Article 74.

st.4: A death sentence passed by a Sessions Judge must be confirmed by the Supreme Court, now under the BNSS, 2023.
st.2: A Gram Nyayalaya is presided over by a Nyayadhikari of the rank of a District Judge.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – the Nyayadhikari is of the rank of a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class; 3 – Gram Nyayalayas are mobile courts at the intermediate panchayat level; 4 – a Sessions Judge's death sentence is confirmed by the High Court.

st.2: Article 323-A deals with public service matters as well as taxation and land reforms.
st.4: Elections to Parliament and State Legislatures, and land reforms, are matters under Article 323-A.
st.3: No hierarchy of tribunals may be created under Article 323-B.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – tribunals under Article 323-A can be set up only by Parliament; 2 – Article 323-A deals only with public service matters; 3 – a hierarchy of tribunals may be created under Article 323-B; 4 – elections and land reforms fall under Article 323-B.

st.3: India, unlike the USA, has single citizenship.

x: All three statements are correct: Uttar Pradesh has 31 Rajya Sabha seats, each US State has two Senators, and India, unlike the USA, has single citizenship.

st.2: The Tarkunde Committee (1974-75) on electoral reforms was a non-official committee appointed by Jayaprakash Narayan.

x: All three statements are correct: the 2023 Act is under challenge in Jaya Thakur, the Tarkunde Committee was a non-official committee set up by Jayaprakash Narayan, and an EC holds office for six years or till 65 with no reappointment.

st.1: It is submitted to the President.

x: Neither statement is correct. The report of a Joint State Public Service Commission is submitted to each Governor concerned, who places it before the State Legislature – not to the President or before Parliament.

st.1: Its Director is appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of a committee of the Prime Minister, the Union Home Minister and the CJI or a judge nominated by him.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – the committee is the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the CJI or his nominee; 3 – the Director of Prosecution is appointed on the recommendation of the CVC, not the CBI Director.

st.2: The Sri Krishna Commission inquired into the 1992-93 Mumbai riots.

x: All three statements are correct: the Bhagwan Sahay Committee saw the Governor as constitutional head and link with the Centre, the Sri Krishna Commission inquired into the 1992-93 Mumbai riots, and Justice M.S. Liberhan headed the Babri Masjid inquiry.

st.3: The Janata Dal was formed on 11 October 1988 by Jan Morcha, Congress (S), Janata and the BJP.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – the Congress for Democracy (1977) was formed by Jagjivan Ram; 3 – the Janata Dal was formed by Jan Morcha, Congress (S), Janata and Lok Dal – the BJP was not part of it.

st.1: The Praja Rajyam Party, founded by Chiranjeevi at Hyderabad in August 2008, won 18 seats in the 2009 Andhra Pradesh election.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. 1 – the Praja Rajyam Party was founded at Tirupati; 2 – it merged with the Congress, not the TDP, in 2011.

st.4: Congress dominance of the Andhra Pradesh party system continued until 1994.
st.2: Uttar Pradesh saw the largest number of coalition governments (nine) in 1967-71.
st.1: After 1967, Kerala was the exception among opposition-ruled States, being governed by a single party alone.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – the exception was Tamil Nadu, ruled by the DMK alone; 2 – the record of nine coalition governments in 1967-71 belongs to Bihar; 3 – the Congress's lowest tally was 26 seats in 1994 (50 in 1985); 4 – Congress dominance ended in 1983 with the TDP's victory.

st.3: In India's experience, fiscal power is the one transferred most fully to local governments.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – incomplete devolution keeps PRIs implementing agencies rather than planning units; 3 – fiscal power is the one transferred least.

st.3: The Grievance Redressal Assessment and Index (GRAI) uses 11 indicators across four dimensions.

x: All three statements are correct: pensioners use CPENGRAMS, the 23 August 2024 circular cut disposal time from 30 to 21 days, and GRAI uses 11 indicators across four dimensions.

st.4: The First ARC recommended institutionalising social audits in all major welfare schemes.
st.2: Tamil Nadu pioneered State-wide social audits of MGNREGA works.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – the first law making social audit mandatory was Meghalaya's (2017); 2 – State-wide MGNREGA social audits were pioneered by Andhra Pradesh; 4 – the recommendation came from the Second ARC (12th Report).

st.1: CERC regulates intra-State electricity matters.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 – CERC regulates inter-State matters, intra-State matters being with the SERCs; 4 – inter-State tariffs are fixed by CERC, not the SERCs.

st.2: SERP, which runs Velugu, is an autonomous society of the Women Development and Child Welfare Department.
st.1: SHGs in Andhra Pradesh are popularly called Kudumbashree groups.
st.4: Under the TDP government Velugu was renamed Indira Kranthi Patham.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – SHGs in AP are called DWCRA groups (Kudumbashree is Kerala's); 2 – SERP is an autonomous society of the Rural Development Department; 3 – SAPAP (1995) was supported by the UNDP; 4 – Velugu was renamed Indira Kranthi Patham under the Congress government.

st.3: Coastal Andhra, not Rayalaseema, is the rain-shadow, drought-prone region.
st.1: Residual Andhra Pradesh holds the deltas of the Godavari, Krishna and Tungabhadra.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – the deltas are of the Godavari, Krishna and Penna (the Tungabhadra is a Krishna tributary with no delta); 2 – AP has 6 agro-climatic zones; 3 – Rayalaseema is the rain-shadow, drought-prone region.

st.3: The private sector was to fund about 39%, the States about 40% and the Centre about 21%.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. 2 – the NIP covers both economic and social infrastructure; 3 – the Centre was to fund about 39% and the private sector about 21%.

st.4: HRIDAY cities are excluded from the list of AMRUT mission cities.
st.2: Its cities cover about 40% of India's urban population.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – AMRUT cities cover about 60% of the urban population; 3 – mission cities are ULBs with 1 lakh or more population, not 50,000; 4 – all HRIDAY cities are AMRUT mission cities.

st.3: Second-hand sales are excluded from national income; only the commission on them is included.

x: All three statements are correct: interest on public debt is a transfer and excluded, resale commission is a payment for a service and included, and the value of second-hand sales itself is excluded.

st.3: Personal disposable income is obtained by deducting personal direct taxes from personal income.

x: All three statements are correct: undistributed profits are deducted and transfer payments added to get personal income, and personal direct taxes are deducted from it to get personal disposable income (corporate tax is deducted earlier, from national income).

st.3: The Census main/marginal worker approach is not one of the NSS status approaches.

x: All three statements are correct: 183 days is the UPS 'major time' line, it separates Census main and marginal workers, and the Census approach is not an NSS status approach.

st.1: Andhra Pradesh's all-age female LFPR (31.7%) is lower than the all-India figure (35.8%) in 2023-24.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. 1 – AP's all-age female LFPR is 35.8%, higher than India's 31.7%; 3 – AP's overall LFPR is higher in rural (50.1%) than urban areas (41.3%).

st.3: The HDR 2016 held economic growth to be the key to human development.
st.1: Mahbub ul Haq extended the capability approach with a list of central capabilities.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. 1 – the list of central capabilities is Martha Nussbaum's; 2 – the four pillars are Equity, Sustainability, Productivity and Empowerment; 3 – HDR 2016 held universalism to be the key.

st.1: It is computed by the Tendulkar method.
st.3: It uses 12 indicators, adding nutrition and bank account to the 10 of the Global MPI.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – it uses the Alkire-Foster method; 3 – the two added indicators are maternal health and bank account (nutrition is already in the Global MPI); 4 – years of schooling is an education indicator.

st.1: The District Planning Committee is provided under Article 243ZE, and four-fifths of its members are elected from the elected members of the district panchayat and municipalities.
st.3: Both these committees are in Part IXA, inserted by the 73rd Amendment (1992).

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – the DPC is under Article 243ZD (243ZE is the MPC); 2 – two-thirds of MPC members are elected; 3 – Part IXA was inserted by the 74th Amendment.

st.3: Special problems carried a weight of 7.5% in the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula.

x: All three statements are correct: the Gadgil formula (1969) gave way to Gadgil-Mukherjee in 1991, Special Category States got 90% grant and 10% loan, and special problems had a 7.5% weight.

st.2: About 20 tonnes of gold in all were pledged or sold.
st.1: The rupee was devalued in two steps (1 and 3 July 1991) to make Indian imports cheaper.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. 1 – the devaluation was meant to make exports cheaper (it makes imports dearer); 2 – about 67 tonnes in all were pledged or sold; 3 – the RBI pledged about 47 tonnes with the Bank of England and the Bank of Japan.

st.2: About 135 million people left multidimensional poverty during 2005-15.
st.1: India's national MPI headcount fell from 55.3% (2005-06) to 14.96% (2022-23).

x: Only statement 4 is correct. 1 – 14.96% was the 2019-21 figure (2022-23 is estimated at 11.28%); 2 – the 135 million exits were during 2015-21; 3 – 'Strategy for New India @75' was released in 2018.

st.1: The present framework of M1 to M4 follows the Chakravarty Committee (1985).

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 – the M1–M4 framework follows the Second Working Group on Money Supply (1977); 4 – the Third Working Group (1998) was chaired by Y.V. Reddy.

st.1: The RBI helped set up NABARD and SEBI.

x: Neither statement is correct. 1 – the RBI helped set up NABARD, IDBI, SIDBI, NHB and EXIM Bank, but not SEBI; 2 – ownership of these institutions later moved to the Government.

st.2: The Standing Deposit Facility, enabled by the Union Budget 2018-19, began in April 2022 as the ceiling of the LAF corridor.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – in October 2026 the MPC moved to calibrated tightening, not accommodative; 2 – the SDF is the floor of the corridor (the MSF is the ceiling).

st.3: The corridor between the SDF and the MSF was 25 bps wide.
st.1: The repo rate was raised to 5.50%.
st.2: The SDF rate was 5.50% and the Bank Rate 5.00%.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – the repo rate was held at 5.25% (it rose to 5.50% only in October 2026); 2 – the SDF was 5.00% and the Bank Rate 5.50%; 3 – the corridor was 50 bps wide; 4 – the floor was the SDF, not the fixed-rate reverse repo.

st.2: Central bank policy rates have no effect on the capacity of banks for credit creation.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – policy rates do regulate banks' capacity for credit creation; 3 – monetary tools act mainly on demand, so supply-driven food inflation needs buffer stocks and supply measures.

st.3: Credit cards, insurance, factoring and mutual-fund distribution are core banking activities, not para-banking.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – since 1 April 2012 a cheque is valid for three months; 3 – these are para-banking activities.

st.3: Deposits with NBFCs are covered by DICGC insurance up to ₹5 lakh.
st.1: The 2018 NBFC liquidity crisis was triggered by defaults at Yes Bank.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. 1 – the 2018 crisis began with IL&FS defaults; 2 – NBFCs cannot accept demand deposits; 3 – NBFC deposits are not DICGC-covered.

st.1: It ended with the Union Budget 2015-16.
st.3: Andhra Pradesh, however, retained it in its 2017-18 Budget.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – the split ended with the Union Budget 2017-18; 2 – it was replaced by the revenue / capital classification; 3 – AP also dropped it from its 2017-18 Budget.

st.2: It gives a fixed subsidy per kg of the fertiliser product, not per kg of nutrient.
st.3: It covers 22 grades of controlled nitrogenous fertilisers.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – NBS fixes the subsidy per kg of nutrient (N, P, K and S); 3 – it covers 22 grades of decontrolled P&K fertilisers; 4 – urea is outside NBS.

st.4: Andhra Pradesh's capital outlay in BE 2026-27 is ₹48,698 crore, a fall of 47% over the previous year.
st.3: Capital outlay is about 83% of Andhra Pradesh's total expenditure in BE 2026-27.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 – it is revenue expenditure that is about 83% of AP's total; 4 – AP's capital outlay of ₹48,698 crore is a rise of 47%.

st.3: Treasury bills form over 90% of the Central Government's debt.
st.2: External debt makes up about 96.7% of public debt.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – it is internal debt that makes up about 96.7% of public debt; 3 – dated Government securities, not Treasury bills, form over 90% of Central debt; 4 – debt is classified as internal or external by the source of borrowing, not maturity.

st.2: It is a multi-stage, origin-based consumption tax.

x: Neither statement is correct. 1 – the taxable event under GST is supply, not manufacture; 2 – GST is destination-based, not origin-based.

st.1: The AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 lists seven agro-climatic zones for AP.
st.3: AP's High Altitude and Tribal zone covers the Rayalaseema uplands.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – APSES 2024-25 lists six zones (seven is the older figure); 3 – the High Altitude and Tribal zone covers the agency areas; 4 – ICAR-NARP has 127 zones (72 sub-zones are the Planning Commission's).

st.3: It has been extended for three years from 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2026.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 – it was extended for five years, to 31 December 2028; 4 – it covers about 81.35 crore people.

st.3: The Johl Committee recommended shifting 20% of the paddy area to other crops.

x: All three statements are correct: Punjab and Haryana extract 35-57% more groundwater than recharge, N:P:K use is skewed at 10.9:4.1:1, and the Johl Committee sought a shift of 20% of the paddy area.

st.3: In 2024-25 AP's rabi paddy yield (6,979 kg/ha) was higher than its kharif paddy yield (5,612 kg/ha).

x: All three statements are correct: foodgrain output was 157.59 lakh tonnes in 2017-18, 2023-24 was the only contraction year (-1.58%), and rabi paddy yield (6,979 kg/ha) exceeded kharif (5,612 kg/ha) in 2024-25.

st.3: It refinances the EXIM Bank and SIDBI for export and industrial credit.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – IFCI was not merged into NABARD (it took over ARDC, ACD and RPCC); 3 – NABARD refinances Scheduled Commercial Banks, RRBs, State Cooperative Banks and Land Development Banks, only for agriculture and rural development.

st.2: Under the original Act, an undertaking was covered if its assets were ₹20 crore or more.

x: All three statements are correct: the Dutt Committee (1969) recommended the Act, the original threshold was ₹20 crore of assets, and the 1984-85 amendment raised it to ₹100 crore.

st.4: Under RBI norms, erosion of net worth alone can never make a micro or small unit sick.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 – under RBI norms an account must stay NPA for more than 3 months, not 6; 4 – 50% erosion of net worth also makes a micro or small unit sick.

st.2: Andhra Pradesh uses Section 70 for institutions that are in no schedule.
st.1: Terms for continuing the facilities of Schedule IX institutions were to be agreed within one year.
st.4: AP Bhavan, New Delhi, is divided according to location, though Telangana claims it as Nizam's property.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – the one-year time limit applies to Schedule X institutions; 2 – AP uses Section 66 for institutions in no schedule (Section 70 governs APSFC); 3 – APSFC is a Schedule IX institution; 4 – AP Bhavan lies outside the State and is divided by population ratio.

st.1: The ADB approved an $800 million loan on 19 December 2024.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – the $800 million loan of 19 December 2024 is the World Bank's; 3 – both loans are disbursed in Japanese yen, not US dollars.

st.2: Its Centre:State sharing for general States is 60:40.

x: All three statements are correct: MIDH began in 2014-15 with NHM and HMNEH as sub-schemes, general States share costs 60:40 (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States), and NHB, CDB and CIH are fully centrally funded.

st.1: In 2023-24 AP ranked second in eggs, with 2,548.74 crore eggs.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – AP ranked first in eggs in 2023-24; 2 – AP ranked seventh in milk in 2023-24.

st.3: The APSADA Act, 2020 licenses only marine cage culture, not freshwater aquaculture.
st.4: Aquaculture farms within 2 km of the High Tide Line come under the APSADA Act, not the Coastal Aquaculture Authority.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – MPEDA functions under the Ministry of Commerce; 3 – the APSADA Act licenses freshwater aquaculture through e-Matsyakar; 4 – farms within 2 km of the HTL come under the Coastal Aquaculture Authority.

st.1: Andhra Pradesh received 860.0 mm of rain in June-December 2024 against a normal of 960.3 mm.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – AP received 960.3 mm against a normal of 860.0 mm; 2 – this was 11.7% above normal, not 16.5%.

st.1: As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, livestock grew at 7.1% and fishing and aquaculture at 8.8%.

x: All three statements are correct: livestock grew at 7.1% and fishing and aquaculture at 8.8%, livestock was about 30.87% of agricultural GVA in 2023-24, and fisheries has grown about 9.08% a year since 2014-15.

st.2: It targets 60 GW+ of clean energy capacity.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – the policy targets 160 GW+; 3 – it targets Net Zero by 2047, not 2030.

st.1: The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 was amended in 1987 with stricter penalties, but noise was kept out of its scope.
st.2: The Environmental Protection Fund Rules, 2026 were made under Section 16 of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – the 1987 amendment also brought noise within the Air Act; 2 – the Rules were made under Section 16 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986; 3 – the compensation powers are under Section 33A of the Water Act and Section 31A of the Air Act, not the other way round.

st.2: The RBI frames the regulations for the issue and listing of municipal bonds.
st.4: The RBI Retail Direct Scheme lets retail investors buy corporate bonds directly from the RBI.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – SEBI frames the municipal bond regulations; 3 – SEBI lowered, not raised, the face value of corporate bonds; 4 – Retail Direct is for G-Secs, not corporate bonds.

st.1: It decreases with latitude.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – the Coriolis force increases with latitude; 3 – it is zero at the Equator and maximum at the poles.

st.3: Melting ice that shifts mass away from the Earth's axis slows down its rotation.

x: All three statements are correct: precession made Vega the pole star about 14,000 years ago, Milankovitch cycles drive long-term climate change, and mass moving away from the axis slows the Earth's rotation.

st.1: The Himalayas are the longest mountain range and the Andes the highest.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. 1 – the Andes are the longest range and the Himalayas the highest; 3 – Cotopaxi (~5,897 m) is slightly higher than Kilimanjaro (5,895 m).

st.3: Norway has the longest coastline in the world.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. 2 – the second-longest border is Russia–Kazakhstan (Chile–Argentina is third); 3 – Canada has the longest coastline, Norway coming second.

st.1: The Great Plains lie west of the Rockies in the USA and Canada.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – the Great Plains lie east of the Rockies; 2 – the West Siberian Plain lies between the Urals and the Yenisei, not the Lena.

st.2: Shikoku is the smallest of the four main islands.

x: All three statements are correct: from north to south the islands are Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu; Shikoku is the smallest; and the Kanto plain is the largest lowland.

st.4: The Danube, Europe's longest river, flows through 10 countries.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 – the Danube rises in the Black Forest of Germany, not the Swiss Alps; 4 – the Danube is Europe's second-longest river, the Volga being the longest.

st.3: The term was coined by Robert Angus Smith in 1872 in Manchester.

x: All three statements are correct: acid rain has a pH below 5.6, it comes mainly from SO₂ and NOx, and Robert Angus Smith coined the term in 1872 from his work in Manchester.

st.3: It recurs irregularly, roughly every 2–7 years.

x: All three statements are correct: El Nino is a warm current replacing the cold Peru current, it is named for the Christ child as it appears around Christmas, and it recurs irregularly every 2–7 years.

st.2: It contains hardly any water vapour or dust, most of which lies in the stratosphere.
st.4: The temperature at the tropopause is about −45°C over the equator and −80°C over the poles.
st.3: The normal lapse rate is about 6.5°C per km, temperature rising with height.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – the troposphere extends to about 8 km at the poles and 18 km at the equator; 2 – it contains nearly all the water vapour and dust; 3 – temperature falls with height at about 6.5°C per km; 4 – the tropopause is about −80°C over the equator and −45°C over the poles.

st.1: About 99% of the mass of the atmosphere lies within 8 km of the surface.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – 99% of the mass lies within 32 km; 3 – moving up, oxygen disappears before nitrogen.

st.3: Neon, helium, krypton, xenon and hydrogen together make up about 1% of the air.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – carbon dioxide is about 0.04%, not 0.4%; 3 – these gases occur only in traces (the remaining ~1% is mostly argon).

st.3: Aurorae occur when charged particles from the Sun excite upper-air atoms near the magnetic equator.
st.4: The MST radar is at the National Atmospheric Research Laboratory at Thumba, near Thiruvananthapuram.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – the ionosphere expands by day and contracts at night; 3 – aurorae occur near the magnetic poles; 4 – the MST radar is at NARL, Gadanki, near Tirupati.

st.3: Palnadu district belongs to Coastal Andhra.

x: All three statements are correct: in the 2022 set of 26 districts Uttarandhra had 6 and Rayalaseema 8 districts, and Palnadu (carved from Guntur) is in Coastal Andhra.

st.3: Cyclone Hudhud (2014) was named by India.
st.2: The May 1996 cyclone caused about 1,000 deaths and was a turning point for disaster management.
st.1: The Diviseema cyclone of 19 November 1987 caused about 10,000 deaths, the maximum in AP.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – the Diviseema cyclone struck on 19 November 1977; 2 – the turning-point cyclone was that of May 1990; 3 – the name Hudhud was given by Oman; 4 – Cyclone Montha struck the Kakinada coast, not Visakhapatnam.

st.3: The Crop Weather Watch Group of the Ministry of Earth Sciences meets weekly during the monsoon.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. 2 – the mandatory indicators are rainfall deviation and dry spells (crop sowing and NDVI are impact indicators); 3 – the Crop Weather Watch Group is of the Ministry of Agriculture.

st.1: The Dowleswaram anicut on the Krishna was built by Sir Arthur Cotton in 1847–1852.
st.4: In October 2022 it became the first ICID World Heritage Irrigation Structure of Andhra Pradesh.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – the Dowleswaram anicut is on the Godavari; 2 – the barrage is at Rajamahendravaram on the East Godavari side; 4 – it was AP's fourth ICID heritage structure, after the KC Canal, Cumbum Tank and Porumamilla Tank.

st.3: The Krishna and Godavari waters are shared by tribunal awards, while the Bahuda and Nagavali are shared by inter-state agreements.

x: All three statements are correct: AP has about 40 rivers (15 inter-state), about 75% of the State lies in the Godavari, Krishna and Pennar basins, and Krishna and Godavari waters are shared by tribunal awards while the Bahuda and Nagavali are shared by agreements.

st.1: The Krishna agro-climatic zone covers Krishna and Guntur districts.

x: All three statements are correct: the Krishna zone covers Krishna and Guntur (Nellore lies in the Southern zone), the Southern zone covers Nellore, Chittoor, Tirupati and parts of Kadapa, and the Scarce Rainfall zone covers Kurnool and Anantapur.

st.2: Bhangar is old alluvium and Khadar is new alluvium.

x: All three statements are correct: alluvium covers the northern plains from Punjab to Assam, Bhangar is old and Khadar new alluvium, and cashew, casuarina and coconut grow on AP's coastal sands.

st.1: Alpine forests occur at high altitudes in the Himalayas, not on the Western Ghats.

x: All three statements are correct: alpine forests are found high in the Himalayas (the eastern slopes of the Western Ghats carry moist deciduous forest), tropical evergreen forests grow in wet and coastal areas, and coniferous forests occupy the temperate Himalayan belt.

st.3: Its personnel come on deputation from the central armed police forces such as the BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP and SSB.

x: All three statements are correct: the NDRF began with 8 battalions and now has 16, each battalion has 18 search-and-rescue teams, and its personnel come from the central armed police forces, not the Army.

st.2: The Prime Minister set out the SAGAR vision in Sri Lanka in 2015.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. 1 – the Draft Blue Economy Policy Framework (2021) was prepared by the Ministry of Earth Sciences; 2 – SAGAR was set out in Mauritius in 2015.

st.2: Emerald is a variety of beryl coloured by chromium.

x: All three statements are correct: ruby and sapphire are corundum, emerald is beryl coloured by chromium (or vanadium), and sapphire's colour comes from iron and titanium.

st.2: The 2015 amendment funded the District Mineral Foundation from contributions paid by mining leaseholders.

x: All three statements are correct: the 2015 amendment made auctions mandatory and created the DMF and NMET, the DMF is funded by miners' contributions (not the Consolidated Fund), and the 2023 amendment let the Centre auction critical minerals and added exploration licences.

st.1: Bhavanapadu, known for heavy-mineral beach sands, is in Visakhapatnam district.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. 1 – Bhavanapadu is in Srikakulam district; 3 – Kurnool is inland and has no beach sands.

st.1: Gondwana coal is about 15-60 million years old.

x: Neither statement is correct. 1 – Gondwana coal is 250-300 million years old (15-60 million years is the age of Tertiary coal); 2 – Tertiary coal is found mainly in the North-East and as lignite; the Damodar valley has Gondwana coal.

st.3: Aseel is a poultry breed.

x: All three statements are correct: Punganur is a cattle breed, Nellore a sheep breed and Aseel a poultry breed.

st.2: Urea is made from ammonia and carbon dioxide, the ammonia being produced by the Haber process.

x: All three statements are correct: naphtha, gas, coal, rock phosphate, sulphur and gypsum are inputs, urea comes from Haber-process ammonia and CO₂, and sulphur for phosphatic fertilisers comes mainly from oil refineries.

st.1: Kakinada is the Andhra Pradesh node of the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – the AP node of the CBIC is Krishnapatnam; 3 – the Amritsar-Kolkata Industrial Corridor is built on the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor.

st.2: Durgapur and Salem were among the alternative sites considered before Visakhapatnam was chosen.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – the alternatives were Bailadila, Goa, Neyveli, Salem and Hospet, not Durgapur; 3 – the first blast furnace was named Godavari.

st.2: Salem is one of its special steel plants.

x: All three statements are correct: SAIL was incorporated on 24 January 1973, Salem is one of its special steel plants (Bhilai is an integrated plant), and its headquarters is in New Delhi.

st.3: Kerala has the highest road density in India.

x: All three statements are correct: India's 63.45 lakh km road network is the second largest, National Highways are about 2% of length but carry about 40% of traffic, and Kerala has the highest road density.

st.4: The State targets port capacity of 300 MTPA by 2030.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 – Visakhapatnam is not one of the four greenfield ports; 4 – the target is 145 MTPA by 2030 (300 MTPA is the 2047 target).

st.3: Its Krishna stretch is Srisailam-Prakasam Barrage.
st.2: Its Godavari stretch is Polavaram-Antarvedi.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – the Godavari stretch is Bhadrachalam-Dowleswaram; 3 – the Krishna stretch is Wazirabad-Prakasam Barrage; 4 – the Buckingham Canal flows through Pulicat Lake, not Chilika.

st.3: Anna FM (2004), India's first community radio station, was licensed by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

x: All three statements are correct: Prasar Bharati (Act of 1990) runs AIR and Doordarshan, Yojana is published by the Ministry of I&B, and Anna FM was licensed by the Ministry of I&B.

st.3: Their number grew from 32.73 lakh in 1971 to 84.69 lakh in 2011.

x: All three statements are correct: SCs numbered 84.69 lakh (17.08% of the State), formed 4.21% of India's SCs, and grew from 32.73 lakh in 1971.

st.1: Srikakulam had the highest sex ratio (1,019) among the districts in 2011.
st.3: West Godavari had the highest child sex ratio (968).
st.2: Kurnool had the lowest sex ratio (977) in 2011.

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 – the highest sex ratio (1,019) was Vizianagaram's, Srikakulam coming second; 2 – the lowest (977) was Anantapuramu's; 3 – the highest child sex ratio (968) was East Godavari's; 4 – the PCPNDT Act was enacted in 1994.

st.2: Maharashtra had the largest number of slum dwellers.

x: All three statements are correct: India's slum population was 6.54 crore (17.4% of urban), Maharashtra had the most slum dwellers, and Greater Visakhapatnam had the highest share among million-plus cities.

st.3: It has been merged into the Code on Social Security, 2020.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – the displacement allowance was 50% of monthly wages; 3 – the Act was merged into the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020.

st.2: DST is the nodal department for the RDI Fund.

st.3: Total R&D funding rose to about Rs 1.33 lakh crore in FY 2023-24.

st.2: India has about 429 legacy dumpsites.

st.4: DAP 2020 made offsets compulsory in government-to-government and single-vendor deals.

st.3: e-Pathshala is CBSE's platform for e-textbooks.

st.4: MeitY's 2nd Digital Threat Report 2025-26 focuses on the power sector.

st.1: N.I. Vavilov identified twelve centres of origin of cultivated plants.

st.3: Cryopreservation can store seeds and pollen but not gametes or embryos.
st.4: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault, in Greenland, keeps seeds in permafrost at about −18 °C.

st.2: The Ministry of Environment and Forests was formed in 1985 and renamed MoEFCC in 2014.

st.1: Coal-based thermal power plants produce fly ash, a biodegradable industrial waste.

st.2: Vermicompost is made by the fungus Trichoderma.

st.1: The National Mission on Natural Farming, approved on 25 November 2024, is a standalone centrally sponsored scheme, not a sub-scheme of PKVY.

st.3: According to the IMD, 2024 was India's warmest year since 1901.

x: All three statements are correct: the 2020 MoES assessment was India's first national climate assessment, India warmed about 0.7°C over 1901-2018, and 2024 was India's warmest year since 1901 (2025 was eighth).

st.2: India is not a member of the Global Methane Pledge launched at COP26.

x: All three statements are correct: the UK's Glasgow Breakthroughs cover power, road transport, steel, hydrogen and agriculture, India has not joined the Global Methane Pledge, and the CCAC targets short-lived climate pollutants.

st.3: Earth Overshoot Day is calculated by UNEP and was conceived by Andrew Simms.
st.1: The ecological footprint is the volume of freshwater needed to produce a population's goods and services.

st.2: Kerala and Uttarakhand jointly topped the 2023-24 edition.

st.3: The 2024 amendments added a 'pandemic emergency' as a new, higher tier above the PHEIC.

st.1: INSPIRE selects young students only through a competitive national exam.

x: Neither statement is correct. 1 – INSPIRE is open to all young students without a competitive exam; 2 – Vigyan Jyoti is for girls of Classes 9-12, not 6-10.

st.3: M.S. Swaminathan received it in 2024, posthumously.

x: All three statements are correct: the slabs became 0, 5, 18 and 40 per cent, the 40% slab covers sin/demerit goods, and individual health and life insurance attract nil GST.

st.2: Russia is one of the eight ADMM-Plus Dialogue Partners.

st.1: ACITI is a technology partnership of Australia, Chile and India.

st.3: Oceans absorb about 90% of the excess heat.

st.3: The IMF's Economic Outlook (June 2026) projected global growth of 2.8%.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. 2 – the theme was under Chapter VII, not Chapter VI, of the UN Mandate; 3 – Pitch Black is hosted by Australia.

st.3: Commercial operation on priority sections of the Mumbai–Ahmedabad HSR is planned for 2030.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. 1 – the Cooperative Biogas for Growth Initiative supports a target of 1,000 plants, not 500; 3 – commercial operation on priority sections is planned for 2027.

st.2: The denial of Sikh jathas to Nankana Sahib in November 2025 was the second such denial in 2025.

st.4: Corporate donations were banned from 1969 to 1985, and the law caps a party's election expenditure.

st.2: The Court directed the ECI to accept Aadhaar as the 12th valid document, as proof of citizenship as well as identity.

st.3: Submergence in Chhattisgarh's Bijapur district was studied by the Central Water Commission.
